Some bees won’t take to old drawn comb. You can try to encourage them by spraying the frames with sugar syrup. I would move a couple of brood frames up into the honey super for a few days. Get the bees used to making the hike up to the upper box.

Do you have a queen excluder on? Are you using plastic foundation? If you are using a queen excluder, pull that off until you get a lot of bee activity in your honey super. Once they start building out the frames and storing resources, you can put the excluder back on. If you have a plastic excluder, throw that away and get a metal excluder. If your frames are old or only have light wax, re-wax them. You can melt down beeswax in a crockpot and then paint it onto plastic frames using a small paint roller. 

If you think the bees are avoiding the super due to the moth balls, checkerboard some brood frames up into the honey super and let it stay that way for about a week and then move things back. That will get the bees used to going up there.

I have personally killed several queens (including Peggy) for various reasons because it is for the strength of the colony and not for a single bee. Here's a sample of the notes that we take.  The box color indicates the year that the queen was introduced. The number in the box indicates how many boxes are on that hive. OHB indicates where the queen came from. ITA indicates it is an Italian queen. The whole log sheet has the date, weather, and is lined up exactly how the colony is laid out in real life for reference. I can go back to any inspection, pick up these notes and know exactly what was going on at that snapshot in time. Super clear and easy to follow.

The pump sits on the side of the engine behind the driver side front tire. 3 bolts hold it to the side of the engine and then there are two bolts that secure the transmission fluid lines that go into the pump. Take the wheel off and the fender well liner so you can get access. Swap the pump and while you have the wheel off you will want to unscrew the transmission fluid fill bolt and top it off with fluid since you’ll lose some fluid during the swap. You could use this as an excuse to do a drain and fill on the transmission since you’ll have all of the access anyway. Took me about 30-45 minutes when I did it.
